title: What Is a Good MYP Standard Mathematics Grade?
summary: Learn what counts as a good MYP Standard Mathematics grade, how internal criteria and eAssessment boundaries work, and how to improve your result.
body_markdown:
A **good MYP Standard Mathematics grade** is generally a **5 or above** on the IB's 1--7 scale. A grade 5 shows secure mathematical understanding and generally successful application, while a 6 is strong and a 7 represents exceptional, consistently sophisticated performance. A grade 4 remains a satisfactory result.


The meaning of a grade depends on whether it is an **internal school grade** or an externally awarded **MYP Standard Mathematics eAssessment** grade. Both use the 1--7 scale, but they are calculated differently. Understanding that distinction helps students set realistic targets and interpret results accurately.


### What each MYP Standard Mathematics grade means


MYP grades are **criterion-referenced** . Performance is judged against published standards rather than ranked against other students, so no fixed percentage of candidates must receive each grade.


Grade Practical interpretation


**7** Exceptional achievement, including comprehensive understanding, sophisticated reasoning, precise communication, and confident application.


**6** Strong achievement showing extensive understanding, effective reasoning, and considerable independence.


**5** Good achievement showing secure understanding and successful application, including some unfamiliar situations.


**4** Satisfactory achievement showing basic understanding and reliable performance in familiar situations.


**3** Developing achievement with partial understanding and continuing gaps or misconceptions.


**2** Limited achievement with significant gaps and inconsistent mathematical work.


**1** Minimal achievement with very limited evidence of understanding.


For most students, **grade 5 is a sensible definition of a good result** . A 6 is a particularly strong target for students considering demanding mathematics or science pathways. A 7 should not be treated as the only successful outcome because it requires consistently excellent performance across several forms of mathematical thinking.


### How internal MYP Mathematics grades are calculated


School-based MYP Mathematics assessment uses four equally important criteria. Each receives an achievement level from **0 to 8** , producing a maximum total of **32** .


Criterion Main focus


**A: Knowing and understanding** Selecting and applying mathematical knowledge and methods


**B: Investigating patterns** Finding patterns, forming general rules, and justifying conclusions


**C: Communicating** Using notation, representations, reasoning, and mathematical language


**D: Applying mathematics in real-life contexts** Modelling situations, interpreting results, and evaluating validity


Teachers make a **best-fit judgment** using the criterion descriptors. A level of 6 out of 8 is therefore not automatically equivalent to answering 75% of an assessment correctly. For final internal reporting, the four levels are added and converted using the general MYP boundaries.


Criterion total out of 32 Final grade


1--5 1


6--9 2


10--14 3


15--18 4


19--23 5


24--27 6


28--32 7


A total of zero normally indicates insufficient evidence. Schools should follow their published assessment policies when selecting evidence and determining final internal grades.


### Worked grade example


Suppose a student receives these levels:


Criterion Level


A 6


B 5


C 6


D 7


**Total** **24 out of 32**


The total of **24** falls within the **24--27** boundary, producing a final grade of **6** . This is a strong MYP Standard Mathematics grade.


The example also demonstrates why balanced performance matters. Procedural accuracy in Criterion A cannot compensate completely for weak investigation, communication, or modelling. Students must show reasoning, justify conclusions, and evaluate results as well as obtain correct answers.


### How the MYP Standard Mathematics eAssessment is graded


The optional **MYP Standard Mathematics eAssessment** is an externally marked on-screen examination taken at the end of MYP Year 5. It can provide an IB-validated course result and contribute Mathematics toward the full MYP certificate.


The current IB subject brief describes a **two-hour** examination organized around three broad tasks:


Task Main assessment focus


Knowing and understanding Mathematical knowledge and methods, mainly Criteria A and C


Investigating patterns Investigation, generalization, interpretation, and communication, mainly Criteria B and C


Applying mathematics in real-life contexts Modelling, interpretation, evaluation, and communication, mainly Criteria C and D


The tasks are normally worth approximately **31--35 marks each** , with Criterion C assessed throughout the examination. All four criteria are equally represented in the overall assessment design.


The examination is first marked using **raw marks** . The IB then applies subject-specific boundaries for that examination session to convert the result into a grade from 1 to 7. Consequently, the internal boundary of **28 out of 32 for a grade 7** must not be applied to an eAssessment paper marked out of approximately 100.


External raw-mark boundaries can change because the IB considers the difficulty of each examination while maintaining a consistent achievement standard. Previous boundaries can support rough estimates, but they do not guarantee a particular outcome in another session.


### Is a grade 4 a good result?


A grade 4 is a respectable result showing basic understanding, reliable work in familiar situations, and some ability to apply mathematics. It is above the MYP certificate's minimum individual eAssessment component grade of **3** .


The certificate also requires at least **28 points out of 56** , a minimum grade of 3 in every required eAssessment component, and completion of the other certificate conditions. A Mathematics grade alone therefore does not determine certificate eligibility.


Students planning advanced mathematical study should examine the criterion profile behind a 4. Weak communication requires different preparation from gaps in algebra, functions, geometry, statistics, or mathematical modelling.


### Standard Mathematics compared with Extended Mathematics


Standard Mathematics develops the core principles needed for further study, while Extended Mathematics adds content and greater breadth and depth. Both report grades from **1 to 7** , but identical grades do not demonstrate identical content coverage.


Course placement should reflect readiness, interests, school policy, and likely Diploma Programme choices. Students should not choose Extended Mathematics only because it appears more prestigious, nor assume that Standard Mathematics prevents later mathematical study. Algebraic fluency, reasoning, independence, and intended subjects are more useful considerations.


### How to improve from a 4 or 5 to a 6


Improvement begins by identifying the weakest **criterion** , rather than completing random questions. A student who performs well in Criterion A but poorly in B or D may understand the syllabus yet struggle to generalize, justify, model, or evaluate.


A useful weekly routine includes:


- one timed set combining accurate methods with unfamiliar problems
- one pattern investigation requiring a justified general rule
- one modelling problem requiring interpretation and evaluation
- one rewritten solution using precise notation and logical steps
- an error log separating conceptual, procedural, communication, and technology mistakes

The broader[Standard Mathematics resource collection](https://www.revisiondojo.com/myp/myp-standard-mathematics) provides additional structured practice.


For examination preparation, students should use complete on-screen-style problems rather than relying only on short calculations. The[30-day MYP eAssessment study plan](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/myp-eassessments-30-day-study-plan) supports timed preparation, while the guide to[how MYP Mathematics is assessed](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/how-myp-mathematics-is-assessed-and-how-to-revise-for-it) explains how to balance Criteria A--D.


### Common mistakes when interpreting grades


A classroom percentage does not necessarily convert directly to the 1--7 scale. Criterion levels come from descriptors and best-fit judgments, so one quiz may provide evidence without determining the final level.


Students should also avoid assuming that every score is simply averaged. Schools use published procedures to select sufficient and often recent evidence. Finally, correct answers alone are insufficient for the highest levels: reasoning, notation, justification, interpretation, and evaluation must be visible.


### Conclusion


A **good MYP Standard Mathematics grade** is usually a **5** , while a 6 is strong and a 7 represents exceptional performance. A grade 4 remains satisfactory, and a grade 3 meets the minimum subject-grade condition associated with certificate eligibility when every other requirement is satisfied.


Internal grades combine four criterion levels out of 32, whereas the external eAssessment uses raw marks and session-specific boundaries. Students improve most effectively by diagnosing criterion-level weaknesses and combining conceptual review with timed, fully explained problem solving.
